answers: The prophets of Israel
The builders of the wall
The women who hunted souls
easy.explanation: The Lord told Ezekiel to prophesy against the prophets of Israel.
easy.q: Against whom was Ezekiel commanded to prophesy?

answers: From the word of the Lord
From their own hearts
From the king's command
easy.explanation: They prophesied out of their own hearts rather than from the Lord.
easy.q: From where did the foolish prophets speak?

answers: Go up into the gaps and make up the hedge
Build a new temple
Gather the people into Jerusalem
easy.explanation: They had not gone up into the gaps or made up the hedge for Israel.
easy.q: What had the prophets failed to do for the house of Israel?

answers: They acted according to their own thoughts
They followed a storm wind
They obeyed the Spirit of the Lord
medium.explanation: They followed their own spirit and had seen nothing from the Lord.
medium.q: What does it mean that the prophets followed their own spirit?

answers: That the Lord had sent them to lead Israel
That their message would confirm the word
That the people would never leave the land
medium.explanation: They made others hope that they would confirm the word, although the Lord had not sent them.
medium.q: What false expectation did the prophets give the people?

answers: A true and certain revelation
An ancient written record
Something empty or without truth
medium.explanation: In this passage, vanity refers to an empty or false vision.
medium.q: What does the word “vanity” mean in “seen vanity”?

answers: They were useless and offered no real protection
They guarded the city from invading armies
They repaired the breaches in Israel's defenses
challenge.explanation: Foxes in ruins suggest destruction and uselessness, matching the prophets' failure to protect the people.
challenge.q: Why is the comparison of Israel's prophets to foxes in the deserts fitting?

answers: Because they spoke truth, they would be honored in Israel
Because they deceived the people, they would lose their place among the people, in Israel's records, and in the land
Because they remained silent, they would be removed from the battle
challenge.explanation: The Lord declares that they will not remain in the assembly, be written among Israel, or enter the land.
challenge.q: What connection is there between the prophets' lies and their punishment?

answers: They said the Lord had not spoken, although the people believed them
They said, “The Lord saith it,” although the Lord had not spoken
They promised war when the Lord had promised peace
challenge.explanation: They claimed divine authority by saying, “The Lord saith it,” even though the Lord had not spoken.
challenge.q: What central contradiction appears in the prophets' message?

paragraphs.title: The Wall and the Plaster of False Hope

answers: A wall
A temple
A written prophecy
easy.explanation: One person built up a wall, and others daubed it with untempered morter.
easy.q: What did the people build that the false prophets covered with plaster?

answers: Tempered mortar
Untempered mortar
Mortar mixed with hailstones
easy.explanation: The prophets daubed the wall with untempered morter, which could not make it strong.
easy.q: What kind of mortar did the prophets use?

answers: It would become stronger
It would remain standing
It would fall and be destroyed
easy.explanation: The shower, hailstones, and stormy wind would cause the wall to fall.
easy.q: What would happen to the wall?

answers: Its covering was weak and could not truly strengthen it
It was built too high for the city
It had no gate through which the people could enter
medium.explanation: Untempered mortar provided only a false covering and no real strength.
medium.q: Why could the wall not stand?

answers: That the prophets had spoken truly
That the vision of peace was false
That Jerusalem had built a better wall
medium.explanation: The destruction of the wall exposed the emptiness of the prophets' vision of peace.
medium.q: What would the fall of the wall reveal?

answers: They covered it with a weak material that gave no real protection
They painted it with a bright color
They removed the stones from its foundation
medium.explanation: To daub with untempered mortar was to hide weakness with an inadequate covering.
medium.q: What is meant by “daubed it with untempered morter”?

answers: It only makes the wall wet
It destroys the wall and exposes the false security it represented
It supplies the materials needed to rebuild the wall
challenge.explanation: The storm destroys the physical wall and reveals that the promised security was baseless.
challenge.q: How does the storm work both literally and symbolically?

answers: The problem was deeper than the outward appearance
The wall was built of precious metal
The prophets had secretly built a stronger wall beneath it
challenge.explanation: The exposed foundation shows that the attractive outer covering had hidden a deeper weakness.
challenge.q: What is suggested when the foundation is discovered after the wall falls?

answers: They opposed every plan made for Jerusalem
They gave false confidence to a plan that had no secure foundation
They repaired the wall after the storm destroyed it
challenge.explanation: The prophets covered the wall with reassuring words even though there was no true peace or protection.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the prophets and the wall?

answers: The builders of the wall
The daughters of Israel who prophesied from their own hearts
The kings of the surrounding nations
easy.explanation: Ezekiel was told to set his face against the daughters of his people who prophesied falsely.
easy.q: To whom did Ezekiel's prophecy turn in this section?

answers: Pillows and kerchiefs
Swords and shields
Books and letters
easy.explanation: They sewed pillows to armholes and made kerchiefs upon heads to hunt souls.
easy.q: What did the women use to hunt souls?

answers: Bless them
Preserve them
Tear them away
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to tear the pillows and kerchiefs from their arms and heads.
easy.q: What would the Lord do to the women's devices?

answers: Head coverings
Weapons of war
Building materials
medium.explanation: The women made kerchiefs upon the head of every stature as part of their deceptive practices.
medium.q: What were the kerchiefs mentioned in the passage?

answers: They polluted the Lord among His people
They destroyed Jerusalem with their own hands
They prevented the people from building a wall
medium.explanation: The Lord said that they polluted Him among His people through their lies and practices.
medium.q: Besides hunting souls, how did the women offend the Lord?

answers: They made the righteous glad and the wicked repent
They saddened the righteous and strengthened the wicked
They released every soul that came to them
medium.explanation: Their lies made the heart of the righteous sad and strengthened the hands of the wicked.
medium.q: What was the moral effect of the women's actions?

answers: They used deceptive spiritual claims to trap souls for very little payment
They served the people without receiving anything
They proved that the people of Israel were wealthy
challenge.explanation: The women profaned the Lord and manipulated lives for small payments of food.
challenge.q: Why does the mention of handfuls of barley and pieces of bread emphasize the seriousness of their deeds?

answers: He would give them new visions
He would tear away their devices, release the souls, and deliver His people
He would build a wall around their houses
challenge.explanation: The Lord would remove their pillows and kerchiefs and deliver the people from their hands.
challenge.q: How would the Lord destroy the women's power?

answers: The women presented a false and distorted judgment of who should live or die
The women accurately knew the future
The women were practicing medicine
challenge.explanation: Their lies reversed true moral judgment, harming the righteous and encouraging the wicked.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between slaying souls that should not die and saving souls that should not live?
